study: Early et al. 2016, Every Classroom Every Day (ECED), IRRE; JREE 9(1)
eval_evidence: Paper states the trial was 'conducted by independent researchers'; authors were university-based (Rochester/NYU/UNC), distinct from IRRE, the program developer.
developer_evidence: PD/support delivered through school-employed instructional coaches and IRRE consultants; the developer IRRE trained coaches rather than the research team delivering PD; coaches 'employed by the school but trained by IRRE'.
cascade_evidence: 'Instructional coaches are employed by the school but trained by IRRE'; IRRE trains the school-based coaches who in turn work with classroom teachers -> a train-the-coach hop.
counterfactual_evidence: Nominal BAU, but 'six of the 10' control schools 'did employ instructional coaches' -> control contaminated with similar coaching practice.
coaching_evidence: Teachers supported through ongoing instructional coaching, weekly meetings, and recurring in-class EAR-Protocol observation/feedback over the two years (school-based coaches trained by IRRE).
student_dose_evidence: ECED delivers a structured literacy curriculum 'in a required, stand-alone class that is in addition to the regular ninth- and tenth-grade English courses, doubling the amount of ELA exposure' -> extra instructional minutes for students.
maturity_evidence: Primary extracted wave = end of Year 2 (end of the 2-year treatment); teachers/coaches had completed >=1 prior implementation year (Year-1 interim wave reported separately).
